pairs.mechanism: Rifampicin induces UGT1A1 and CYP3A, lowering dolutegravir exposure.
pairs.effect: Lower dolutegravir levels; risk of HIV treatment failure and resistance.
pairs.management: Dolutegravir dose frequency is adjusted while on rifampicin and for a period after stopping; see source. Avoid if integrase resistance is known or suspected.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Dolutegravir-based first-line ART is national policy; TB/HIV co-treatment is common. Uganda HIV guideline 2022 has a TB drug interaction section (p.163) and a DTG with TPT section (p.170) not yet read.

pairs.mechanism: Chelation by polyvalent cations reduces dolutegravir absorption.
pairs.effect: Large fall in dolutegravir levels when taken together.
pairs.management: Separate the doses; the source gives the timing window. Avoid with integrase resistance.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Antacids are widely bought over the counter; patients may not report them.

pairs.mechanism: Chelation with calcium when taken fasting.
pairs.effect: Lower dolutegravir levels if taken together on an empty stomach.
pairs.management: Take together with food, or separate the doses; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Calcium is given in pregnancy; many women in antenatal care take dolutegravir.

pairs.mechanism: Chelation with iron when taken fasting.
pairs.effect: Lower dolutegravir levels if taken together on an empty stomach.
pairs.management: Take together with food, or separate the doses; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Iron and folic acid are routine in antenatal care alongside dolutegravir.

pairs.management: Separate the doses; see source. Food effect unknown.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Zinc is used for childhood diarrhoea; children may be on dolutegravir.

pairs.management: Prefer a non-interacting anticonvulsant; if no alternative, dolutegravir dosing is adjusted; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Epilepsy and HIV commonly coexist; carbamazepine is a common first-line anticonvulsant.

pairs.management: FDA label: avoid (insufficient data to give a dose). UCT sheet: use alternative anticonvulsant; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Phenytoin is used for seizures and status epilepticus in hospitals.

pairs.management: FDA label: avoid (insufficient data). Consider an alternative anticonvulsant; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Phenobarbital is a low-cost anticonvulsant used in adults and neonates.

pairs.mechanism: Dolutegravir inhibits renal OCT2 and MATE transporters that clear metformin.
pairs.effect: Higher metformin levels; more side effects.
pairs.management: Review metformin dose and monitor; the sources give dose limits; see source. Monitor renal function.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Diabetes is rising among people on long-term ART; Uganda HIV guideline 2022 Figure 40 covers metformin (not read).

pairs.mechanism: Herbal enzyme induction lowers dolutegravir exposure.
pairs.management: Avoid co-administration (FDA label).
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Herbal use alongside ART is common in Uganda (see herbal findings).

pairs.effect: Weekly rifapentine: possible reduced dolutegravir effect. Daily rifapentine: not to be combined.
pairs.management: Weekly rifapentine with standard dolutegravir: monitor virological response; daily rifapentine: do not co-administer; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: 3HP TB preventive therapy is used with DTG-based ART; Uganda guideline section on DTG and TPT (p.170) not yet read.

pairs.mechanism: Rifampicin strongly induces CYP3A, lowering lopinavir exposure.
pairs.effect: Loss of HIV control; higher-dose strategies raise liver and gut toxicity.
pairs.management: FDA label: contraindicated. Liverpool: avoid unless strictly necessary; some guidelines allow an adjusted regimen with liver monitoring; see source. Consider rifabutin-based TB treatment.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Lopinavir/ritonavir remains in second-line and paediatric regimens; sources disagree, so the signed rule needs a pharmacist decision.

pairs.mechanism: Strong CYP3A induction lowers atazanavir exposure.
pairs.effect: Loss of HIV control and resistance.
pairs.management: Do not combine; use rifabutin-based TB treatment per HIV/TB guidance; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Atazanavir/ritonavir is a second-line option.

pairs.mechanism: Strong CYP3A induction lowers darunavir exposure.
pairs.management: Do not combine; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Darunavir/ritonavir is used in third-line ART (Uganda guideline Table 82, not read).

pairs.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid lowers atazanavir absorption.
pairs.effect: Lower atazanavir levels; risk of treatment failure.
pairs.management: Avoid or follow the label's acid-reducer rules; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Omeprazole is widely available; on the ONC high-priority list.

pairs.mechanism: Ritonavir inhibits CYP3A, raising simvastatin levels.
pairs.management: Do not combine; choose a statin the source allows; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Statin use is growing in people on long-term ART.

pairs.effect: Acute ergot toxicity: vasospasm and ischaemia.
pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ergometrine/methylergometrine are used in obstetrics; check which ergot products are on the formulary.

pairs.management: Label: do not co-administer.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Legacy and infant prophylaxis use of nevirapine.

pairs.management: Sources differ on dose change (FDA label vs SAHCS 2023); see source. Pharmacist decision needed.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Efavirenz-based regimens persist for some patients with TB.

pairs.management: Label: use an alternative anticonvulsant.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Epilepsy with HIV.

pairs.mechanism: Efavirenz induces CYP3A4, lowering artemether, dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine.
pairs.effect: Lower antimalarial levels; possible reduced efficacy.
pairs.management: Use with caution; monitor malaria response.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ugandan PK study showed lower lumefantrine with efavirenz; AL is first-line for uncomplicated malaria.

pairs.management: Counsel; consider a method not affected (e.g. DMPA or IUD) or add barrier; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ugandan study (Scarsi 2016) found unintended pregnancies with this combination.

pairs.management: Label: use a reliable barrier method in addition.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Family planning integration in HIV clinics.

pairs.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 induction lowers artemether and lumefantrine.
pairs.effect: Large falls in antimalarial levels; risk of treatment failure.
pairs.management: Do not combine; choose an alternative antimalarial per national guidance.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ugandan study (Lamorde 2013) showed marked falls; TB and malaria co-occur.

pairs.management: Do not combine; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Epilepsy patients treated for malaria.

pairs.management: Do not combine; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: As above.

pairs.management: Avoid giving other antimalarials with AL unless no option; use quinine cautiously after AL; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Severe malaria pathways may overlap parenteral and oral antimalarials.

pairs.mechanism: Additive QT effect; lumefantrine inhibits CYP2D6.
pairs.management: Label: should not be given together.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Amitriptyline is used for neuropathic pain and depression, including in HIV care.

pairs.management: Label: avoid co-administration.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Quinine is used for severe malaria and in pregnancy; TB co-treatment possible.

pairs.management: Label: avoid macrolides during quinine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Macrolides are common antibiotics.

pairs.effect: Treatment failure for schistosomiasis or other worms.
pairs.management: Do not combine; see source for timing.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Schistosomiasis treatment and mass drug administration are common in Uganda.

pairs.mechanism: Rifampicin induction lowers contraceptive hormone levels.
pairs.management: Advise a non-hormonal or unaffected method; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Women on TB treatment.

pairs.mechanism: Induction of CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 lowers warfarin levels.
pairs.effect: Reduced anticoagulation; clot risk; rise in INR when rifampicin stops.
pairs.management: Monitor INR closely when starting and stopping; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Warfarin users with TB.

pairs.management: Review fluconazole dosing; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Cryptococcal disease and TB in advanced HIV.

pairs.management: Monitor for withdrawal; dose review by prescriber; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Methadone-assisted treatment programmes; TB in people who use drugs.

pairs.management: Review steroid dosing; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Steroids are given in TB meningitis and pericarditis.

pairs.management: Monitor blood glucose.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: TB and diabetes co-occur.

pairs.management: Expected co-prescription in standard TB regimens; monitor for hepatotoxicity. Candidate for information-only display.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Fixed-dose TB regimens contain both; an interruptive alert here would be noise.

pairs.management: Monitor for toxicity and levels if available.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: TB preventive therapy and treatment in people with epilepsy.

pairs.management: Avoid if possible or monitor INR closely; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Co-trimoxazole is widely used in HIV care.

pairs.management: Monitor INR closely; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Metronidazole is very commonly prescribed.

pairs.management: Monitor prothrombin time and INR closely.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Fluconazole is used for candidiasis and cryptococcal disease.

pairs.management: Monitor INR closely.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Macrolides are used for respiratory infection and H. pylori.

pairs.management: Monitor INR and bleeding.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ciprofloxacin is commonly prescribed.

pairs.management: Monitor INR closely; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Atrial fibrillation care in referral hospitals.

pairs.mechanism: Additive bleeding risk (antiplatelet and gastric effects).
pairs.management: Avoid where possible; monitor closely.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: NSAIDs are widely bought over the counter.

pairs.management: Use together only when indicated; monitor closely.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Cardiac patients may need both.

pairs.mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel.
pairs.management: Label: avoid omeprazole or esomeprazole; consider another acid reducer.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Gastroprotection is commonly co-prescribed.

pairs.management: Avoid if possible; monitor blood counts if needed.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Co-trimoxazole prophylaxis is common; methotrexate used in rheumatology and oncology.

pairs.mechanism: Xanthine oxidase inhibition reduces azathioprine/mercaptopurine breakdown.
pairs.management: Label requires azathioprine dose reduction; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Gout patients on immunosuppressants; oncology.

pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: On the ONC high-priority list; check formulary status.

pairs.management: Check potassium on starting or changing either; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Common in heart failure care.

pairs.management: Label: generally stop potassium supplements in heart failure when starting spironolactone.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Potassium supplements are common on wards.

pairs.management: Monitor potassium.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: As above.

pairs.management: Monitor potassium.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Co-trimoxazole is common in HIV care.

pairs.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion and blunt ACE inhibitor effect.
pairs.effect: Kidney injury in elderly or dry patients; weaker blood pressure control.
pairs.management: Monitor renal function, especially if volume depleted.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Over-the-counter NSAID use in hypertensive patients.

pairs.management: Monitor lithium levels frequently.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Check lithium availability on formulary.

pairs.management: Do not combine; hold the statin or choose another antibiotic.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Clarithromycin is used in H. pylori regimens.

pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Itraconazole is used for fungal infections in advanced HIV.

pairs.effect: Higher myopathy risk at higher statin doses.
pairs.management: The label sets a simvastatin dose limit; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Common combination in hypertension and cardiovascular risk care.

pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Migraine and obstetric ergot use.

pairs.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition raise colchicine.
pairs.effect: Life-threatening colchicine toxicity; contraindicated in renal or hepatic impairment.
pairs.management: Avoid; contraindicated with renal or hepatic impairment; label requires colchicine dose reduction otherwise; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Gout care; renal impairment is common.

pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Nitrates in cardiac care; sildenafil also used in pulmonary hypertension.

pairs.management: Avoid if possible; monitor for serotonin syndrome.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Tramadol is a common analgesic; SSRI use is growing.

pairs.management: Do not use within 14 days of an MAOI (label).
pairs.ugandaRelevance: MAOIs are rare; linezolid is an MAOI-type drug (see linezolid pairs).

pairs.effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death.
pairs.management: Avoid where possible; if needed, use lowest doses and monitor (boxed warning).
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Common on wards and in emergency care.

pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: On the ONC high-priority list.

pairs.mechanism: Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor.
pairs.management: Monitor closely for serotonin syndrome; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Linezolid is part of drug-resistant TB regimens.

pairs.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition and additive QT prolongation.
pairs.management: Do not combine.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Both are common antimicrobials.

pairs.mechanism: Additive QT prolongation (class effect stated by source).
pairs.effect: Torsades de pointes and sudden death.
pairs.management: Avoid combining where possible; consider ECG and electrolytes.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Many common drugs prolong QT (antimalarials, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, some antipsychotics); a class rule needs a signed list of member drugs.

pairs.management: Label: avoid; monitor serum levels if unavoidable.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Aminophylline is used for asthma and COPD.

pairs.management: Separate the doses; see source for timing.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Antacids, iron and zinc are common.

pairs.management: Measure digoxin levels; label advises digoxin dose reduction; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Heart failure and atrial fibrillation care.

pairs.mechanism: Calcium potentiates digoxin effect on the heart.
pairs.effect: Serious arrhythmias if given rapidly IV.
pairs.management: Avoid rapid IV calcium in patients on digoxin; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: IV calcium is used for hyperkalaemia and hypocalcaemia.

pairs.effect: Fatal precipitates in lungs and kidneys in neonates.
pairs.management: Contraindicated in neonates (up to 28 days) who need IV calcium; in others do not give simultaneously; see source.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Ceftriaxone is a first-line antibiotic for neonatal and child sepsis; Ringer's lactate contains calcium.

pairs.management: Generally not recommended; if needed, consider other anticonvulsant cover.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Meropenem use is rising for resistant infections.

pairs.management: Label: avoid concurrent use.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Gentamicin is widely used in neonatal and adult sepsis.

pairs.mechanism: In vitro CYP3A4 inhibition, P-gp effects and PXR activation (no clinical data).
pairs.effect: Unknown in patients; possible change in ARV levels.
pairs.management: Ask about herbal use; record it; no specific action. Evidence is in vitro only.
pairs.ugandaRelevance: Herbal use with ART reported in 34% to 46% of Ugandan HIV patients, mostly undisclosed.

gaps: Uganda Consolidated HIV guidelines 2022 (S62): only the front matter and table of contents could be read. The tool truncates the PDF at about 30 pages, and the proxy blocks direct download from prepwatch.org and medbox.org. Interaction sections not read: 4.4.2 and Table 19 (ART and contraceptives, pp.92-93); 5.4.1 and Table 40 (ART and TB, pp.163-164); DTG and TPT (p.170); Table 57 (hypertension medicines, p.195); Table 60 (antidepressants, p.202); Table 82 (third-line ART, p.281). Every HIV pair here rests on FDA labels, Liverpool, UCT MIC, NYSDOH and SAHCS sources, not the Uganda text.
Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 and EMHSLU 2023: not opened. Formulary presence of each drug in these pairs is unverified.
Uganda national TB and leprosy manual (current edition): not opened.
WHO consolidated TB and HIV guidelines (interaction annexes): not opened. NCBI and PMC pages returned a browser check and could not be read.
Phansalkar 2013 list of 33 non-interruptive DDIs: only the abstract and count were read; the list itself was not opened.
Payne 2015 seven core alert elements: only the abstract was read; the seven elements are not listed in what was opened.
Strom 2010 and Powers 2018 were read through secondary summaries (Health Exec, PSNet), not the full papers.

Commercial KB prices: none published on any vendor page opened (Wolters Kluwer Lexidrug and Medi-Span, FDB, Merative Micromedex, DrugBank, MedicinesComplete). Pharmaceutical Press data-licensing page failed to load. DrugBank pricing page not opened.
Liverpool TB or antimalarial-specific interaction resources: not confirmed; the Liverpool page opened names HIV, hepatology and COVID-19 only.
DDInter full terms on commercial use and redistribution were not visible beyond the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement.

Several FDA labels used are repackager copies with old revision dates (efavirenz 2013, nevirapine 2010, clarithromycin 2012, quinine 2013, allopurinol 2009). A pharmacist should check each against the current innovator label or Uganda NDA-approved product information.
FDA labels reflect US products and doses, not NDA Uganda registrations. NDA product information was not consulted (www.nda.or.ug was blocked by the session proxy).

Herbal-drug interaction evidence for Ugandan herbs is thin: usage surveys and one small RCT (S58-S60), plus African in vitro data (S61). No Ugandan herb-specific pharmacokinetic interaction pairs could be sourced.
Paediatric-specific interaction handling (weight-based DTG dosing with rifampicin, LPV/r in children with TB) was not researched beyond label statements.
